name: Great Forge
summary: At Ironforge’s center, the Great Forge keeps its fires burning and smiths at work. Its Great Anvil draws people from across the mountain city.

sections.title: Heart of the Mountain
sections.body:
The Great Forge was the first structure the early dwarves built beneath Ironforge Mountain. The capital grew outward in rings around it. Molten stone and slag run from giant foundries through glowing channels, lighting the cavern with an amber haze.

At the center, Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury oversees the massive Great Anvil. Masters of metalwork gather around its rim to hammer armor, tools, and weapons day and night.

sections.title: Hub of the Alliance
sections.body: Smithing is only part of the Great Forge’s work. Guild offices, supply shops, and the city’s main gryphon roost ring the chamber. Gryth Thurden tends the roost, where travelers from across the Alliance mingle amid the hammer blows.

faq.q: Why is the city named after this forge?
faq.answer: The Great Forge was the first part of the settlement the dwarves carved beneath the mountain. As the halls spread outward from its central chamber, they named the city Ironforge for the great furnace at its heart.

faq.q: What notable items have been created here?
aliases: what was made at the great anvil
faq.answer: Dwarven smiths have made generations of weapons and armor on the Great Anvil, including historic masterpieces. The forge’s fires have never been allowed to go cold.
Myolor Sunderfury directs the Great Forge’s daily work and upkeep as Keeper of the Great Forge.

faq.q: Why is it always so crowded here?
aliases: why so many people at the forge
faq.answer: The Great Forge lies at Ironforge’s center and connects to the outer ring and nearby districts. Its crafting trainers, shops, and central gryphon roost draw citizens, couriers, and travelers through the chamber.

angles.text: The Great Anvil is the Alliance’s foremost smithing site, with high-ranking trainers at the heart of the city.
For dwarves, the Great Forge is the foundation of civilization beneath the mountain. Its fires keep centuries of smithing tradition alive.
